Feature architecture

Clean Architecture

Generate a feature-first module that separates external data access, business contracts, and presentation code while leaving application-specific operations for your team to define.

Generate a feature

kite --feat:clean dashboard

Canonical forms:

kite feature dashboard --architecture clean
kite feature dashboard --clean

Generated structure

lib/features/dashboard/ ├── data/ │ ├── dtos/ │ │ └── dashboard_dto.dart │ ├── repositories/ │ │ └── dashboard_repository_impl.dart │ └── sources/ │ └── dashboard_remote_source.dart ├── domain/ │ ├── entities/ │ │ └── dashboard_entity.dart │ ├── repositories/ │ │ └── dashboard_repository.dart │ └── usecases/ │ └── get_dashboard_use_case.dart └── presentation/ ├── providers/ │ └── dashboard_providers.dart ├── screens/ │ └── dashboard_screen.dart └── widgets/ └── dashboard_content.dart

Layer boundaries

D

Domain

Immutable entities, repository contracts, and use cases. No UI, networking, database, or framework dependencies.

A

Data

Remote or local sources, DTOs, serialization, repository implementations, and DTO-to-domain mapping.

P

Presentation

Manual Riverpod providers, controllers or notifiers, screens, and reusable feature-owned widgets.

✓

Compile-safe placeholders

Contracts are intentionally minimal. Kite does not assume endpoints, parameters, or business methods.

Add routing

kite --feat:clean dashboard --route

Kite creates a feature route file and updates its managed route registry. Handwritten router composition remains separate from Kite-owned generated route entries.

Add JSON serialization

kite --feat:clean dashboard --json

The DTO uses json_annotation and a generated part file. After adding real fields:

dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs

Example provider flow

final dashboardRemoteSourceProvider = Provider<DashboardRemoteSource>(
  (ref) => const DashboardRemoteSourceImpl(),
);

final dashboardRepositoryProvider = Provider<DashboardRepository>(
  (ref) => DashboardRepositoryImpl(
    remoteSource: ref.watch(dashboardRemoteSourceProvider),
  ),
);

final getDashboardUseCaseProvider = Provider<GetDashboardUseCase>(
  (ref) => GetDashboardUseCase(
    repository: ref.watch(dashboardRepositoryProvider),
  ),
);
i
Why the interfaces are empty

Feature generation cannot know whether your dashboard loads one endpoint, combines multiple repositories, streams data, or has no remote source at all. Empty contracts give you the correct boundaries without inventing the wrong API.
